intended_object: The inclusion map U ↪ V between two open subsets U ⊆ V of a topological space α, sending x ∈ U to x viewed as an element of V. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body is just `Set.inclusion h`, applied to the underlying sets of the opens U and V, with `h : U ≤ V` read as `(U : Set α) ⊆ V`. So it is exactly the inclusion map between the open sets, viewed as subtypes. The docstring describes it as a convenience wrapper: it states `Set.inclusion` with `Opens` arguments directly, so that users do not have to rely on definitional unfolding of the coercion. It reuses the general Mathlib construction rather than rebuilding it. Restricting it to `Opens` is the purpose of the wrapper, not an unnecessary loss of generality, since the general version `Set.inclusion` already exists and is what it calls. There are no degenerate cases where it goes wrong. The verdict is faithful.
